issue.title: gaia-core-candidate lacks the real gaia_engine package -- runs a stale gaia_common.engine shim instead, blocking smoke tests
issue.symptom:
Found 2026-10-14/15 while verifying cjja's premise with a full promotion
dry-run (./scripts/promote_pipeline.sh --dry-run --services gaia-common,
gaia-mcp,gaia-core). Stage 3 (ruff/mypy/pytest validation) is now clean
-- see cjja's own notes for that fix. Stage 4 (20-test cognitive smoke
battery against the candidate) failed hard: only 5/20 passed, 15 failed,
almost all with generic "missing expected keywords" at a suspiciously
uniform ~3.0s.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed directly: gaia-core-candidate's embedded engine
process does NOT have the gaia_engine package importable at all --
`docker exec gaia-core-candidate python3 -c "import gaia_engine.core"`
raises ModuleNotFoundError. The container's actual embedded-engine
traceback (docker logs) shows it running
/gaia-common/gaia_common/engine/manager.py instead -- i.e. the
"backward-compat shim" CLAUDE.md describes as delegating to the real
gaia_engine package is NOT delegating in this candidate at all; it's a
standalone implementation with its own (older/un-synced) copy of the
manager logic.

CONCRETE SYMPTOM: this shim's manager.py lacks a known, already-landed
fix in the real gaia_engine package (gaia_engine/manager.py's
health_response(): "When inference is in flight, skip the proxy. The
worker uses a single-threaded HTTPServer... so /health would queue
behind /v1/chat/completions. For long requests... this caused doctor
health checks to time out... Manager-level state is sufficient for
liveness; detailed per-token info isn't worth the head-of-line
blocking.") Reproduced directly: `docker exec gaia-core-candidate curl
http://localhost:8092/health` took over 120 SECONDS to return (eventually
answered correctly: status=ok, model_loaded=true, device=cpu,
worker_pid=19) -- consistent with health checks queuing behind slow
in-flight generation on a single-threaded server, exactly the problem
the real package already solved. main.py's own readiness gate
(process_packet, ~line 1037) hits this same slow/queued /health and,
when it doesn't get a timely answer, returns a canned "One moment — my
inference engine is loading" stub instead of processing the real
request -- reproduced directly via curl against /process_packet,
returned the canned stub twice in a row even though gaia-core-candidate's
OWN wrapped /health (port 6416, not the embedded engine's 8092) reported
"healthy"/"inference_ok": true at the same time. This mismatch between
the wrapper's reported health and the embedded engine's actual
responsiveness is exactly the smoke test's failure mode.

NOT caused by tonight's t0f2 fix (cuda_health_snapshot/manager.py
changes) -- confirmed cleared: that code lives in the real gaia_engine
package, which isn't even importable in this container, so it isn't
running here at all. Also unrelated to .claude/rules/docker.md's
documented gaia-engine single-file-mount behavior: docker-compose.yml
mounts gaia-engine files into PRODUCTION containers only;
docker-compose.candidate.yml has no such mounts at all (candidates get
gaia-engine baked at image build time, per project memory) -- meaning
this candidate's image was built at some point BEFORE gaia_engine
existed as an installable package, or its build never installs it at
all. Needs investigation: check candidates/gaia-core's Dockerfile for
whether/how it's supposed to install gaia_engine, and when the candidate
image was last actually rebuilt vs. when gaia_engine was extracted to
its own repo (per project memory: "project_engine_extraction.md").

Did not fix tonight -- this is real additional scope (Docker image
build/dependency investigation) discovered while doing cjja's validation
work, not something to chase blind at this hour. cjja itself: Stage 3
validation is genuinely clean and that fix has landed; this bead is what
blocks Stage 4 and therefore full promotion.

regression_test.format: pytest functions added by the fix
regression_test.gold:
# candidates/gaia-core/tests/test_prompt_builder_itws.py
"""Regression test for GAIA_Project-itws: casual turns should keep the
already-existing felt "Body:" vitals line (_somatic_state() in
gaia_common/utils/world_state.py) instead of trimming it out alongside the
raw operational telemetry it was never a part of (GAIA_Project-7n3's gate).
Pins: the line survives on a greeting-intent turn with CASUAL_SOMATIC_ENABLED
on (the default), and is trimmed back out with it off (the kill-switch).
"""
from gaia_common.protocols.cognition_packet import CognitionPacket, Content, Intent
from gaia_core.utils import prompt_builder


def _joined(messages):
    return " ".join(str(m.get("content", "")) for m in messages)


def _greeting_packet():
    return CognitionPacket(
        content=Content(original_prompt="Good morning GAIA"),
        intent=Intent(user_intent="greeting"),
    )


def test_casual_turn_keeps_body_line_by_default():
    messages = prompt_builder.build_from_packet(_greeting_packet())
    assert "Body:" in _joined(messages)


def test_casual_turn_drops_body_line_when_flag_disabled(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("CASUAL_SOMATIC_ENABLED", "0")
    messages = prompt_builder.build_from_packet(_greeting_packet())
    assert "Body:" not in _joined(messages)

diff --git a/candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/utils/prompt_builder.py b/candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/utils/prompt_builder.py
index d2354b7..731026c 100644
--- a/candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/utils/prompt_builder.py
+++ b/candidates/gaia-core/gaia_core/utils/prompt_builder.py
@@ -699,22 +699,33 @@ def build_from_packet(packet: CognitionPacket, task_instruction_key: str = None,
             world_state_block_content = ""
 
     # For personal/chitchat turns (e.g. "how are you?"), strip the OPERATIONAL
-    # world-state lines — uptime/load/mem, immune system, lifecycle "Recent
-    # Events", model paths, self-knowledge. Otherwise GAIA reads her *state* off
-    # the monitoring snapshot and answers like an ops console ("clean run, no
-    # escalations, last sleep cycle, waking circle, running laundry on the
-    # consciousness stack") instead of as herself. Keep only the clock and the
-    # "Context: in Discord" line — harmless and useful, no ops vocabulary.
+    # world-state lines — raw uptime/load/mem numbers, immune system, lifecycle
+    # "Recent Events", model paths, self-knowledge. Otherwise GAIA reads her
+    # *state* off the monitoring snapshot and answers like an ops console
+    # ("clean run, no escalations, last sleep cycle, waking circle, running
+    # laundry on the consciousness stack") instead of as herself.
+    #
+    # itws (2026-10-15): "Body:" and "Lifecycle:" are kept too, unlike the rest
+    # of the operational block above — they're not raw telemetry, they're
+    # ALREADY rendered as felt, declarative facts (_somatic_state() in
+    # world_state.py: "Body: running easy"/"working hard, under load", and the
+    # "Lifecycle ≠ biography" framing on the gearbox-state line), the same
+    # register that already works for Locality's weather line and the Inner-
+    # weather felt-line. Flagged (CASUAL_SOMATIC_ENABLED) so this can be killed
+    # without a redeploy if live use shows it reintroducing 7n3's status-report
+    # narration after all.
     try:
         _ws_intent = (getattr(getattr(packet, "intent", None), "user_intent", "") or "").lower()
         if world_state_block_content and _ws_intent in {
             "chat", "greeting", "farewell", "gratitude", "smalltalk", "social",
             "chitchat", "acknowledgment", "affirmation",
         }:
-            _keep = ("Clock:", "User's local time", "Context:")
-            _trimmed = [l for l in world_state_block_content.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith(_keep)]
+            _keep = ["Clock:", "User's local time", "Context:"]
+            if os.environ.get("CASUAL_SOMATIC_ENABLED", "1").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
+                _keep.extend(["Body:", "Lifecycle:"])
+            _trimmed = [l for l in world_state_block_content.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith(tuple(_keep))]
             world_state_block_content = "\n".join(_trimmed)
-            logger.info("PromptBuilder: trimmed world-state to clock/context for personal intent '%s'", _ws_intent)
+            logger.info("PromptBuilder: trimmed world-state to %s for personal intent '%s'", _keep, _ws_intent)
     except Exception:
         logger.debug("world-state personal-trim failed", exc_info=True)
